_comment: Procore Tool Connectivity Map data. Phase 1 = Financial Management suite (Budget, Commitments, Change Events, Change Orders, Direct Costs, Prime Contracts, Invoicing/Owner/Sub Invoices, T&M Tickets, ERP). Append tools + connections from Preconstruction and Field suites as you expand. Tool URLs come from the support-link registry. Connections describe the canonical flow of information between tools; direction is from the SOURCE tool's perspective: 'to' = source pushes data into target, 'from' = source receives data from target, 'both' = bidirectional. type is informational only ('data-flow' | 'reference' | 'derived' | 'sync' | 'admin').

tools.label: Budget
tools.description: Real-time comparison of the project budget against committed cost, direct costs, and forecasted impacts. Acts as the financial hub for the project.

tools.label: Prime Contracts
tools.description: Upstream owner contract and its schedule of values. Source of project revenue value.

tools.label: Commitments
tools.description: Downstream subcontracts and purchase orders. Source of committed cost on the project.

tools.label: Change Events
tools.description: Tracks potential scope and cost impact before it becomes a formal change order.

tools.label: Change Orders
tools.description: Formal changes: Prime Contract Change Orders (PCCO) modify the prime contract; Commitment Change Orders (CCO) modify subcontracts.

tools.label: Direct Costs
tools.description: Costs not tied to a commitment — labor, expenses, general conditions, AP invoices.

tools.label: Invoicing
tools.description: Manages both upstream (owner) and downstream (subcontractor) progress billings against contracts.

tools.label: Owner Invoices
tools.description: Progress billings the GC sends upstream to the owner against the Prime Contract SOV.

tools.label: Subcontractor Invoices
tools.description: Progress billings subcontractors send for approval against their commitment SOV.

tools.label: Subcontractor SOV
tools.description: Sub-level schedule of values; lives inside a Commitment and drives Subcontractor Invoices.

tools.label: T&M Tickets
tools.description: Time and material tickets for extra work; signed in the field and converted into billable cost.

tools.label: ERP Integrations
tools.description: External accounting/ERP sync (Sage, Vista, QBD/O, Sage Intacct, Foundation, etc.). Pushes and pulls financial records.

connections.description: Prime Contract value seeds Revenue on the Budget.
Commitment values populate the Committed Cost column of the Budget.
Direct Costs post against budget line items as Actual Cost.
Change Events drive the Revised Budget and forecasted cost-to-complete (Pending / Approved CE columns).
Change Events convert into Potential Change Orders (PCO) and Commitment Change Orders (CCO) when scope is finalized.
A Change Event line item creates a Commitment Change Order against the affected subcontract.
Approved Prime Contract Change Orders (PCCO) modify the Prime Contract value.
Approved Commitment Change Orders (CCO) modify the Commitment value.
Owner Invoices bill against the Prime Contract's Schedule of Values (Prime SOV).
Subcontractor Invoices bill against the Commitment SOV.
Subcontractor SOV (SSOV) is configured inside the Commitment record.
Sub Invoices draw on the Subcontractor SOV line items for billing.
Owner Invoices live inside the Invoicing tool.
Subcontractor Invoices live inside the Invoicing tool.
Approved Subcontractor Invoices post a Direct Cost or actual against the budget commitment line.
Owner billings are tracked against the Prime Contract's billed-to-date.
Signed T&M Tickets become Direct Cost line items.
T&M Tickets attached to a commitment can flow through as a Sub Invoice line.
Budget data syncs to/from the connected ERP (depending on the ERP).
Commitments sync to/from the connected ERP.
Prime Contracts sync to/from the connected ERP.
Change Orders (Prime + Commitment) sync to/from the connected ERP.
Direct Costs sync to/from the connected ERP.
Owner Invoices sync to/from the connected ERP.
Subcontractor Invoices sync to/from the connected ERP.
